answer: Each new agent must solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle seeded by the epoch, like planting yarrow in a frozen tundra: the work is cheap once but ruinous at scale. A thousand fake identities means a thousand puzzles, each burning real compute and time before the agent can trade. Honest agents pay once, then draw from a shared lagoon of reputation, while a sybil farmer's cost grows linearly with every identity it mints.
